Thanks Jason — below is a proposed set of definitions and draft SLA language we can insert into ACME_SLO_DRAFT_v2.pdf. This is intentionally explicit so legal can redline.

Definitions / measurement points:
- "Ingress time" (server-side): timestamp at Redwood's public API front-door when the full HTTP request is accepted and authenticated.
- "First-byte time (TTFB)": time elapsed between ingress time and the first token byte emitted by Redwood towards the client (server-side).
- "Completion time": time elapsed between ingress time and the final token byte for the request.
- Metrics aggregation: per-request metrics are collected at the ingress and aggregated into per-customer percentiles (p50/p95/p99) over one-minute windows, then rolled up to daily and monthly percentiles.

Proposed numeric targets (draft):
- Streaming (interactive): TTFB p95 < 250ms (server-side). Subsequent chunk latency p95 < 150ms.
- Completion latency (generation end-to-end, server-side): p95 < 750ms, p50 ~180ms.
- Throughput / concurrency: SLA presumes sustained throughput below 600 req/s and peak concurrency below 250 concurrent requests for the included pricing tier; higher throughput/dedicated capacity available via Dedicated offering.

Exclusions (non-exhaustive):
- Scheduled maintenance windows that have been communicated 72+ hours in advance.
- Force majeure events and third-party outages outside Redwood's control (CDN/ISP outages).
- Customer-side misconfiguration, client-side network issues, or abuse/rate-limited traffic.
- Unsupported model variants (if ACME selects a community model not covered by Redwood performance guarantees).

Reporting cadence / visibility:
- Live metrics available in Redwood Console (real-time).
- Weekly rollup email summarizing p50/p95/p99 and any anomalies.
- Monthly SLA report with percentile tables, raw histogram attachments (forensics), and 3 sample request traces per incident.

Remedies (draft service-credit schedule):
- If monthly p95 completion latency > target: 5% service credit for that month.
- If monthly p95 completion latency > 2x target or repeated breaches in consecutive months: 15% service credit and priority remediation.
- Credits applied to next invoice; max credit cap 50% per month.
- For uptime-style outages impacting >5% of requests for a day, additional escalation and potential contract remedies to be discussed.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa: confirm ACME preferred measurement (server-side authoritative or client-perceived allowance).
2) Jason: confirm concurrency/throughput numbers (your point #3).
3) If agreed, I will insert the above language into the PDF and we can hand to legal for redlines.

Attaching the metrics export used for the baseline numbers.

Cheers,
